issue_paraphrase: Pixel values that scale past the maximum during conversion of a semi-transparent image are not clamped: instead of saturating to the brightest value, they wrap around and come out dark and corrupted. The wrong result depends on the alpha channel, so colors are visibly inconsistent across pixels, and the output silently differs from what an equivalent 8-bit path produces. The fix is a small clamp in one arithmetic path.
fix_summary: In the fast uchar->uchar unpremultiply path, clamp the computed value (in[i]*scale + 128) >> 8 to UCHAR_MAX before storing, fixing a regression introduced by 6fcce4c (Resolves #5182).
notes: Very small, deterministic, no network, no fixtures (image built in memory). The relevant assertion was appended to the pre-existing test_unpremultiply method in the fix commit, so overlay the fix's test/test-suite/test_conversion.py onto the parent tree. NOTE for authors: libvips soname filenames change between release eras (libvips.so.42.20.0 vs 42.21.0); a stale .so with the old symlink can silently shadow a fresh build — after rebuilding, delete /usr/local/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libvips.so* / libvips-cpp.so* then re-run ninja install + ldconfig, and verify the installed .so with strings before trusting results. Test suite needs pyvips compiled against the built libvips (python3-dev required).

issue_paraphrase: Starting a flood-fill drawing operation at a point outside the image (past the right or bottom edge) is silently ignored - the call returns success and nothing is drawn, so callers get no signal that their coordinates were invalid. Negative coordinates fail too, but with an opaque 'parameter not set' property error rather than a clear out-of-bounds message. After the fix the operation reports an explicit out-of-bounds error.
fix_summary: Add an explicit bounds check in vips_draw_flood_build: if the start point x >= Xsize or y >= Ysize, fail with 'start point out of image' instead of silently doing nothing.
notes: Deterministic, no network, no fixtures. NOTE for authors: this commit is from the 8.18.0 era and builds libvips.so.42.20.0 while newer-era commits build libvips.so.42.21.0; meson leaves the old soname file and symlink in place, so a stale .so (containing the fix) can shadow the parent build and make the parent look fixed. After building the parent, delete /usr/local/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libvips.so* and libvips-cpp.so*, re-run ninja install + ldconfig, and verify with `strings <libvips.so> | grep -c 'start point out of image'` (must be 0 at parent). Then overlay the fix's test_draw.py onto the parent tree to run the regression test.

issue_paraphrase: Applying an ICC profile transform to a 32-bit float image whose RGB values are in the usual 0..1 range produces an entirely black result, while the identical image stored as 8-bit bytes transforms correctly. The user-visible symptom is a black image with no indication that the transform failed, and no error is raised.
fix_summary: Use lcms per-channel float pixel formats for float input (FLOAT_SH path via a new vips_icc_make_lcms_format helper) instead of casting float input to uchar before the transform and clipping 0..1 values to 0. Also refactors the profile-signature table to use lcms pixel-type constants.
notes: Requires lcms2 (liblcms2-dev); needs the in-repo fixtures images/sample.jpg and images/sRGB.icm (both tracked in test/test-suite/images, no network). The diff is ~120 lines (within the 4-400 window). Watch the soname issue described in the other entries (8.19.0 builds 42.21.0; the parent here is 8.19.0 so same filename, but check .so content anyway).
